about: Every number the decisions module can be tuned by, with its default. decisions/Settings.ps1 reads this table and nothing else holds a copy. Each entry: kind (text, whole-number, fraction, true-false or folder), default, least and most (the range a value may be in; for text, its fewest and most characters), and means (what it is, in a sentence).

decisions.store.sequenceDigits.means: How many digits a record's file name has. This is the format of the store on disk, not a preference: records written under one width are not records under another, so it is changed only for a store that has none. It is in this table so that the width is written in one place.

decisions.store.maxGap.means: The largest run of missing records that is believed. A file named further than this past the last record before it is a stray, not a record.

decisions.store.heldReadTries.means: How many times a reader tries a record that another process holds open before it reports the record as busy.

decisions.store.heldReadWaitMs.means: How long a reader waits between two such tries, in milliseconds. Tries times wait is how long one read waits for one held record: 2 seconds by default.

decisions.store.leftoverMinAgeSeconds.means: How old a writer's temporary file must be, in seconds, before the next writer may remove it - and then only if no process holds it open.

decisions.write.raceTries.means: How many times one write tries for the next place in the order, each try lost to another writer, before it says it cannot.

decisions.write.heldReads.means: How many reads in a row may find a record held open by another process before a write gives up. Each read has already waited the store's own time, so by default a write waits about 10 seconds.
